entry.notes: Reviewed 2026-07-27 (supersedes the 2026-07-20 review with a fresh measurement and new backstop evidence). The Parallelizer Module documentation establishes a basket conversion mechanism rather than a debt CDP: USDp is minted and burnt at oracle value against a DAO-whitelisted asset set with adaptive fees that widen as an asset depegs or exposures breach target bounds, and any holder can redeem at any time for a proportional share of the backing basket, with a dynamic penalty factor applied when the system collateral ratio falls below 100% so redemptions re-collateralize the system. The mechanism therefore has no borrower debt positions and no liquidation engine; liquidationMechanics and the liquidation capacity metric are structurally not applicable. MEASURED 2026-07-27 ~22:52 UTC: Parallel's server-rendered transparency inventory publishes per-asset reserve values summing to 2,055,279.68 USD (Ethereum: frxUSD 251,516.15, sfrxUSD 478,747.92, USDe 48.45, sUSDe 104,949.32; HyperEVM: sUSDe 522,175.30, USDeOFT 28,695.76; Base: sUSDS 77,515.19, USDS 21.61, USDC 4.00; Avalanche: ygamiUSDC 576,451.58, USDC 15,154.39) against a published total USDp supply of 1,976,343.74, a backing ratio of 1.039940 (down from 1.040064 on 2026-07-20). The reported collateralization ratio is an observed issuer-dashboard measurement, not a vault TCR. External anchors this review: (1) pinned eth_call totalSupply reads across all eight deployment chains (Ethereum 25627275, Base 49201858, Avalanche 91391171, HyperEVM 41619438, Arbitrum 488406161, Optimism 154797144, Sonic 76609019, Sei 222617726) sum to 1,976,338.49 USDp, within 5.3 of the dashboard figure; (2) the Ethereum Parallelizer diamond at block 25627275 returned getCollateralList = [frxUSD, sfrxUSD, USDe, sUSDe] (matching the dashboard's Ethereum basket) and getCollateralRatio = 1.007832280 with 828,660.97 stablecoins issued tracked by the instance, implying ~835,151 USD of Ethereum-instance collateral versus the dashboard's 835,261.85 Ethereum reserve figure (0.013% apart, oracle-timing noise). The whitelisted basket, per-asset exposure targets, and adaptive fee schedule are documented and on-chain verified, supporting adequate collateralization parameters. Permissionless anytime proportional redemption at oracle value supports adequate structural redemption, subject to the documented whitelist caveat for restricted collateral assets. The documented below-100% redemption penalty is a socialized, fee-based recapitalization path rather than an insurance fund, and pause/guardian powers sit with DAO governance and a team multisig, supporting limited shutdownAndBadDebt. NEW backstop evidence: the Parallel Insurance Fund (ratified MIP-28, updated PGP-31) is documented with itemized assets (vlAURA 1,113,709.10, Aura-ECLP PAR/paUSD LP positions, VaultsCore minimums of 10,000 PAR and 1,000 paUSD per V2 chain) and named per-chain multisigs; the DAO has approved covering Parallel V3 USDp deployments on Ethereum, Base, Sonic, HyperEVM, and Avalanche up to 100% of the fund via the bug bounty program. The Ethereum fund multisig 0x6aF71a3723D3c0Ed69f84EE259c9De3019C2a77c was verified on-chain at block 25627275 holding 17,855.61 USDC and 0.0936 WETH. This is issuer-published structured data with an on-chain anchor, supporting limited backstop — not adequate, because coverage is discretionary (DAO-multisig administered and routed through the bug bounty program rather than contractually automatic into the Parallelizer), largely legacy-token-denominated, the verified liquid stable float is small relative to the ~2.06M USD backing, and the vlAURA/LP itemization was not independently verified in this review. NOT established: the isolation between per-chain Parallelizer baskets sharing one fungible USDp — the Proof of Solvency page documents that each chain's Parallelizer holds its own backing, but no loss-isolation or cross-chain rebalancing mechanism is documented, so branchIsolation remains bounded-unknown; and the freshness bounds or failover behavior of the underlying Chainlink/RedStone/DIA feeds, which are scored under oracle risk.

entry.notes: Reviewed 2026-07-27 (replaces the 2026-07-20 review; measurements refreshed and the backstop gap resolved). K3's technical documentation establishes sBOLD as a standard-conforming ERC-4626 vault whose underlying asset is BOLD, deployed across Liquity V2 Stability Pools at pre-configured basis-point weights; collateral gains from liquidations are quoted in real time and swapped to BOLD through a SwapAdapter with a documented minimum-quantity formula (max slippage, reward and swap fee each capped at 10%), and deposit/withdraw preview rounding always favors the vault. Measured on-chain at Ethereum block 25627256 (2026-07-27T22:52:23Z) via eth_call: totalAssets() = 7,719,437.630014434 BOLD, totalSupply() = 7,176,569.116245205 sBOLD, convertToAssets(1e18) = 1.075644574 BOLD per share, and asset() confirms the underlying is BOLD (0x6440F144b7e50D6a8439336510312d2F54BeB01D). The wrapper originates no borrower debt and operates no collateral-ratio liquidation branches, so both CDP metrics and the collateralization and liquidation components remain structurally not applicable; liquidation execution is inherited from the parent BOLD system (variantOf bold-liquity, reviewed separately). BACKSTOP (adequate; newly graded): the wrapper itself adds no backstop and none is disclosed — the complete K3 documentation index (design, introduction, technical details, interactions, price oracle, audit reports, brand assets) and the deployed contract's function inventory contain no insurance, reserve, or recapitalization module — but sBOLD's deposits ride inside Liquity V2's per-branch Stability Pools, the parent's two-stage backstop of Stability Pool debt burn followed by same-branch redistribution. Measured from Liquity's own protocol stats API at 2026-07-27T22:56:39Z: total Stability Pool deposits of 20,879,166.75853167 BOLD against total BOLD supply of 29,607,199.86821610 give an inherited liquidation coverage of 70.5%, above the 0.658 level graded adequate for bold-liquity; the vault's on-chain sps() reads at block 25627256 confirm allocation into the three canonical Liquity V2 Stability Pools, providing the external on-chain anchor for the API figures. BRANCH ISOLATION (adequate; upgraded from limited): the prior review held that the configured weights were not published; K3's introduction page in fact documents the initial 60% wstETH / 30% WETH / 10% rETH allocation under biweekly admin rebalancing, and on-chain sps() reads at block 25627256 verify the live weights remain 30% WETH (pool 0x5721cbbd64fc7ae3ef44a0a3f9a790a9264cf9bf), 60% wstETH (pool 0x9502b7c397e9aa22fe9db7ef7daf21cd2aebe56b), 10% rETH (pool 0xd442e41019b7f5c4dd78f50dc03726c446148695). Liquity V2 keeps liquidation and redistribution losses within each collateral branch, but unrecovered bad debt in any branch transmits to the shared BOLD claim and hence to sBOLD's NAV, which prevents a strong rating. SHUTDOWN AND BAD DEBT (limited): K3's exchange-rate documentation conditions the compounding-share behavior on 'no bad debt from unsuccessful liquidations', i.e. unsuccessful-liquidation losses pass through to the share rate with no wrapper-level cure, and the parent Liquity V2 design has no unconditional recapitalization facility. STRUCTURAL REDEMPTION (limited): redemption is a standard ERC-4626 redeem, but the redeemed value depends on oracle-quoted collateral conversion executed by K3's mutable solver/swap infrastructure under admin control, and the interactions documentation states deposit and withdraw operations are restricted whenever accumulated collateral exceeds the configured maximum-collateral boundary, so redemptions can be temporarily gated under heavy liquidation flow.
